input.rationale: Section 13.5 expressly designates two Customer-payable amounts as liquidated damages: the Termination for Convenience Fee (11.1) and the Termination for Cause Fee (11.2(A)), each a percentage of the "Estimated Remaining Value" (remaining months multiplied by the Monthly Base Fee/average monthly Fees). That fails the fallback on every material term: there is more than one liquidated amount, the amount is measured by the full remaining term rather than three months' fees, and the Cause Fee is triggered by any Customer Event of Default or even a mere failure to give the 11.1 notice — i.e. a minor breach, which is walk-away territory. We therefore capped the early-termination fee at three months' fees, removed the Termination for Cause Fee (conforming the dangling 13.4 reference in 11.2(A)), and stated in 13.5 that the early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer. We target the fallback rather than preferred deletion because removing the fee entirely would require collateral rewrites of the 11.1 payment mechanics. This finding addresses only the fee's character and quantum, not the termination-for-convenience right itself (T4C).
